(frog-cie)=
# frog-cie

<!-- Generated by generate_readme.py from the CLI definitions in src/frogchem/cli. Do not edit by hand. -->

{bdg-warning}`Spectroscopy & grids` Place emission/absorption spectra on the CIE 1931 chromaticity diagram.

## What it does

The colour of an emitter (OLED, fluorescent dye) or of an absorbing sample is reported in papers as
CIE 1931 chromaticity coordinates (x, y): two numbers that place the colour on the standard
horseshoe-shaped colour diagram. This command converts spectra (measured or simulated) into (x, y),
prints them and draws all of them on the diagram, so you can compare compounds, check how close an
emitter is to a target colour, or compare with literature values.

## How it works

```{include} _parts/frog-cie/how_it_works.md
```

## Input

One **CSV file per spectrum** with a header row, a wavelength column in **nm** (default name
`wavelength`) and an intensity column (default name `intensity`); other names are given with
`--wl` and `--int`. The spectrum should cover the visible range (about 380–780 nm); parts outside
it do not contribute. Choose what the intensity means with `--spectrum-type`: an **emission**
spectrum (any intensity scale), an **absorbance** A (as measured, so its absolute size matters),
or a **transmittance**/reflectance between 0 and 1. A simulated spectrum from
`frog-tddft --uv --save-spectra` works too: use `--wl Wavelength_nm --int <curve column>` (it is
normalised to a maximum of 1, i.e. treated as absorbance 1 at the peak). Requires the optional
package `colour-science` (`pip install colour-science`).

### Arguments

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `inputs` … | required | CSV spectrum files (glob patterns allowed) |

**Options**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--wl` `WL` | `wavelength` | Name of the wavelength column (nm) |
| `--int` `INT` | `intensity` | Name of the intensity column |
| `--spectrum-type` `{emission,absorption,transmittance}` | `emission` | How to read the intensity column: 'emission' = emitted spectral power (integrated without illuminant), 'absorption' = absorbance A, converted to T = 10^-A and viewed under D65, 'transmittance' = T (or reflectance) in 0-1, viewed under D65 (default: emission) |
| `--external-coordinates` `CSV` |  | CSV file with extra points to mark (columns Name, CIEx, CIEy) |

| `--ylabel` `TEXT` |  | Label of the y axis |

| `--linestyle` `{solid,dashed,dotted,dashdot}` |  | Line style |
| `--legend`, `--no-legend` |  | Show or hide the legend (default: decided by the plot) |
| `--grid`, `--no-grid` |  | Show or hide the grid (default: decided by the plot) |
| `--figsize` `W H` |  | Figure size in inches |
| `--font-size` `PT` |  | Base font size in points (titles and labels scale with it) |

| Argument | Default | Description |

Shared by every command: `-v/--verbose`, `-q/--quiet`, `--format {table,json,csv}`, `--table-file PATH` — see [CLI conventions](conventions.md).

## Output

| Kind | Name | When | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Terminal | `CIE coordinates` | always | One row per spectrum: CIE 1931 x and y chromaticity coordinates |
| Plot | `cie_diagram.png` | always | CIE 1931 chromaticity diagram with one point per spectrum (path from -o/--output) |

### How to read it

A table with one row per spectrum: **CIE x** and **CIE y** (0–1, 4 decimals), and the diagram with
one dot per spectrum drawn in its own sRGB colour (reference points as crosses).

* Emission (`emission`): the spectrum is integrated directly with the 2° standard observer, so only
  its **shape** matters. A narrow band gives a point close to the curved edge (pure, saturated colour);
  broad or multiple bands move it towards the white region (x ≈ y ≈ 0.31–0.33).
* Absorption/transmittance: the light transmitted under daylight (illuminant D65) is used, i.e. the
  **perceived colour of the sample**, which is the complementary of what it absorbs (absorbing blue
  ⇒ looks yellow). Here the size of A matters: a weak absorber stays close to white.
* Spectra with a step other than 1, 5, 10 or 20 nm are interpolated to 1 nm (info message).
  A file with wrong column names is skipped with a warning; if nothing can be converted the command
  stops with an error.

Example (synthetic Gaussian bands): emission at 520 nm (σ 20 nm) → x 0.1468, y 0.6902 (green);
emission at 620 nm, 2 nm step → x 0.6706, y 0.3292 (red); absorbance 1.0 at 450 nm (σ 30 nm) with
`--spectrum-type absorption` → x 0.4160, y 0.4748 (yellow).

## Step by step

1. Emission: `frog-cie em1.csv em2.csv` (wildcards like `spectra/*.csv` are accepted) → table of x, y and `cie_diagram.png` in the current folder.
2. Colour of an absorbing solution or film: `frog-cie uv.csv --spectrum-type absorption` (or `transmittance` if the column is T).
3. Add literature or target points with `--external-coordinates ref.csv` (columns `Name`, `CIEx`, `CIEy`); change the plot name/format with `-o colours.pdf`, open it with `--show`.

## Full reference

Every option, as printed by `frog-cie --help`:

:::{dropdown} `frog-cie --help`
```text
usage: frog-cie [-h] [-v] [-q] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--table-file PATH] [--wl WL]
                [--int INT] [--spectrum-type {emission,absorption,transmittance}]
                [--external-coordinates CSV] [-o PATH] [--fig-format {png,svg,pdf,eps}]
                [--dpi DPI] [--show] [--title TEXT] [--xlabel TEXT] [--ylabel TEXT]
                [--xlim MIN MAX] [--ylim MIN MAX] [--colors COLOR [COLOR ...]] [--linewidth W]
                [--linestyle {solid,dashed,dotted,dashdot}] [--legend | --no-legend]
                [--grid | --no-grid] [--figsize W H] [--font-size PT]
                inputs [inputs ...]

Place emission/absorption spectra on the CIE 1931 chromaticity diagram.

Each CSV spectrum is converted to CIE 1931 xy chromaticity coordinates with colour-science (2°
standard observer) and drawn on the diagram in its sRGB colour. --spectrum-type selects the
physics: 'emission' (default) integrates the emitted spectrum directly; 'absorption' converts the
absorbance to T = 10^-A and 'transmittance' uses T as given, both viewed under the D65 illuminant
(perceived colour of the sample). Spectra with a non-standard wavelength step are interpolated to
1 nm. Requires `pip install colour-science`.

positional arguments:
  inputs                        CSV spectrum files (glob patterns allowed)

options:
  -h, --help                    show this help message and exit
  --wl WL                       Name of the wavelength column (nm) (default: wavelength)
  --int INT                     Name of the intensity column (default: intensity)
  --spectrum-type {emission,absorption,transmittance}
                                How to read the intensity column: 'emission' = emitted spectral
                                power (integrated without illuminant), 'absorption' = absorbance
                                A, converted to T = 10^-A and viewed under D65, 'transmittance' =
                                T (or reflectance) in 0-1, viewed under D65 (default: emission)
  --external-coordinates CSV    CSV file with extra points to mark (columns Name, CIEx, CIEy)

plot options:
  --fig-format {png,svg,pdf,eps}
                                Image format, unless the path already has an extension (default:
                                png)
  --dpi DPI                     Raster resolution of saved plots (default: 300)
  --show                        Also open the plot in an interactive window
  --title TEXT                  Plot title ('' removes it)
  --xlabel TEXT                 Label of the x axis
  --ylabel TEXT                 Label of the y axis
  --xlim MIN MAX                Range of the x axis
  --ylim MIN MAX                Range of the y axis
  --colors COLOR [COLOR ...]    Colours of the plotted series, in order (matplotlib names or #hex)
  --linewidth W                 Line width in points
  --linestyle {solid,dashed,dotted,dashdot}
                                Line style
  --legend, --no-legend         Show or hide the legend (default: decided by the plot)
  --grid, --no-grid             Show or hide the grid (default: decided by the plot)
  --figsize W H                 Figure size in inches
  --font-size PT                Base font size in points (titles and labels scale with it)

output:
  -v, --verbose                 Enable debug output
  -q, --quiet                   Suppress banner, info and saved-file messages
  --format {table,json,csv}     Format of the tables printed on stdout (default: table)
  --table-file PATH             Also write all tables to PATH (.json, .csv or .txt; otherwise the
                                --format is used)
  -o PATH, --output PATH        Plot path (extension overrides --fig-format)

outputs:
  terminal (stdout; --format table|json|csv, --table-file PATH):
    CIE coordinates             One row per spectrum: CIE 1931 x and y chromaticity coordinates
  plots (saved, not shown; --fig-format, --dpi, --show):
    cie_diagram.png             CIE 1931 chromaticity diagram with one point per spectrum (path
                                from -o/--output)

examples:
  frog-cie spectra/*.csv
      Coordinates of every spectrum and cie_diagram.png
  frog-cie emission.csv --wl nm --int counts -o emission_cie.pdf
      Custom column names, save as PDF
  frog-cie uv_abs.csv --spectrum-type absorption
      Perceived colour of an absorbing sample (T = 10^-A under D65)
  frog-cie *.csv --external-coordinates literature.csv --show
      Also mark reference points (columns Name, CIEx, CIEy) and open the plot window

Data go to stdout, messages to stderr. Atom indices are 0-based unless stated otherwise.
Step-by-step guide (what it is for, what you need, what to expect): docs/cli/frog-cie.md.
```
